name: Banaue Town Center (Poblacion)
tagline: The practical base for buses, supplies, and guides
description: The compact commercial heart of Banaue, where the bus terminal, market, ATM, tourism office, and most inns and restaurants cluster along the main road. It is the least scenic part of the municipality but the most functional, and nearly every trek or village visit starts here with arranging a guide or transport.
cons: can feel like a transit stop rather than a destination

name: Batad Village
tagline: The amphitheater terraces reachable only on foot
description: A remote village built into a natural bowl of rice terraces, accessible by a 30 to 45 minute walk from the road after a van or tricycle ride to the junction. Batad has no road access to the village itself, limited electricity hours, and essentially no signal, but it offers arguably the most spectacular terrace views in the region and access to Tappiya Falls.
cons: no signal and very limited power

name: Banaue Viewpoint (Native Village / Kilometer 4)
tagline: The postcard overlook of the Banaue terraces
description: A hillside viewpoint a short tricycle ride above town, offering the classic panoramic shot of the Banaue rice terraces cascading down the valley, alongside small souvenir stalls selling Ifugao woodcarvings and weavings. It is the easiest terrace view for anyone short on time or unable to trek into Batad or Hapao.
pros: dramatic terrace views with minimal effort
cons: can feel touristy compared to the villages
less immersive than staying in a terrace village

name: Hapao and Hungduan
description: A cluster of villages south of Banaue known for the Hapao and Hungduan rice terraces, including the distinctive spider-web-shaped Hungduan terraces, along with natural hot springs near Hapao. Reached by a longer, rougher van or habal-habal ride, this area sees far fewer tourists than Batad, making it a good option for travelers wanting terraces without the crowds.
bestFor: escaping crowds, hot springs, slower cultural immersion
